records.researcher_notes: The Polk County permits issued December 20, 2024 list 96 Cummins QSK95-G9 engines for the Ginger East site at 1475 SE Maffitt Lake Road: 20 in permit PR-000720-2024 (EP-102 to EP-121) and 76 in permit PR-000722-2024. GEM has 40 engines. The state permit defines Ginger East as emission units 101 to 201. Permit PR-000720-2024 also covers 20 engines at the separate Willow Creek site, and only its Ginger East part is counted here. The permits do not say how many are built. GEM already has 3 MW per engine on this unit, and the state Title V permit gives 3,000 kilowatts for this engine, so only the count changes.

verifications.note: Iowa DNR construction permits for project 26-275, issued October 20, 2026, to Microsoft at 11100 Booneville Road. The description says modification of limits for 126 existing engines and installation of 10 new engines.

records.researcher_notes: The newest state construction permits, project 26-275 issued October 20, 2026, cover 136 engines. Of these, 130 are Cummins QSK95 engines and 6 are Cummins QSX15 engines. Ten engines were added in this project. GEM has 120 large engines. The October 20, 2026 state permits add 10 Cummins QSK95 engines to the 120 in GEM. That makes 130 engines and 390 MW. The 6 Cummins QSX15-G9 engines (755 bhp each) in the same project are not counted, because they are small and I did not find a kilowatt rating for them.

records.plant_name: Microsoft Ginger West Data Center power station

verifications.note: Iowa DNR construction permits for project 26-275, issued October 20, 2026, to Microsoft at 11100 Booneville Road. The description says modification of limits for 126 existing engines and installation of 10 new engines.

records.researcher_notes: The 130 QSK95-G9 engines are 4308 horsepower each in the state permits, which does not give a kilowatt figure. The Cummins product page for the C3000D6e generator set, which uses the same QSK95-G9 engine, rates it at 3,000 kilowatts. That gives 3 MW each, or 390 MW. GEM has 360 MW and already uses 3 MW per engine. I did not find a Ginger West Title V listing with kilowatts, so the 3 MW rests on the Cummins page for the same model. The 6 small QSX15-G9 engines are not counted.
